findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _tainted (`s["stepId"] not in repairers and any(c in tainted for c in s["consumes"])`) and _overridden (the `repairers` of a parent's FAIL; `_fail_scope(v, holders[0], s["seq"], frozenset(failed_by[b]))`); README 'A FAIL crosses the delegation boundary', third bullet
findings.finding:
The repairer exemption waives the whole consumption edge for a delegation whose child FAILed the bytes. That includes the delegation's consumption of steps the FAIL covers only as derived from those bytes, for example a model step built on the failed artefact. Nothing checks the child against those derived bytes. The child can FAIL the original, repair it or not, build its delivered artefact on its own copy of the derived bytes, and the parent builds on the delegation. One loop refuses the same steps.
- K1001: d consumes patch (X) and m2 (N, built on X). Its child FAILs X with unit-tests, makes no repair, and delivers O built on its copy of N. final builds on d. Accepted by rounds 5 to 10. The one-loop controls are refused: K1001c (o consumes m2) and K1001d (o consumes a fresh copy of N after the FAIL, through the copy edge).
- K1002: K1001 where the child also repairs X to Y, passing every gate, and builds O on Y and N. Accepted.
- K1003: K1001 under K821, with the parent's own unit-tests FAILing X after d. Accepted since round 9; round 8 refused it because d was covered.
- K1004: d consumes only m2 (N); its child regenerates X and FAILs it. Accepted.
- K1005 (control): K1003 without the child's FAIL is refused, so the exemption is what lets these through.
- K1006: a valid form in which the child's revision itself reads N (a revision may consume covered bytes) and is delivered. Accepted, as in one loop (K1006c).
The README justifies the exemption as follows: 'it carries the child's repair, which the parent may build on ... since that FAIL's gate must pass the repair in the child'. That does not hold here, because the delegation's artefact is built on covered derived bytes, not only on the repair. 'Not claimed' names derived bytes that a later child regenerates without consuming them (C702). It does not name a delegation that consumes covered steps and is exempt.

findings.location: README 'A FAIL crosses the delegation boundary', the paragraph 'Only passes inside the child count for a child's revision. This fails closed in two cases that one loop accepts: ...'
findings.finding:
The rule is stated accurately, and the two named cases (G901d and H906b) are refused as stated. The list of cases is not complete, though. The same rule refuses other loops that one loop accepts:
- J1001: the parent's failing gate passes the delegation's Y after the delegation but before the FAIL. The README names only a pass 'after the FAIL'. One loop accepts it (J1001c).
- J1002: the parent's failing gate passed the same bytes Y on an earlier holder, before the delegation. In one loop an earlier gate on the same bytes counts (J1002c).
- J1003: the parent's own later FAIL, not a sibling's. The parent never uses d and repairs the patch itself; the child's delivered revision never passed unit-tests. One loop accepts it (J1003c). This case is new in round 10 (rounds 8 and 9 accept it). The README's second case names only 'a later sibling's failing gate'.
- J1004: a sibling child's pass of the same bytes.
J1001, J1002 and J1004 were also refused by round 8 and accepted by round 9.
findings.requiredChange: State the class instead of 'two cases'. For example: 'This fails closed wherever one loop would count a pass outside the child: in the parent or a sibling, before or after the FAIL, on the delegation's artefact or on another holder of the same bytes. It also fails closed wherever the child delivers a revision that a later FAIL in the parent or a sibling covers, even if the parent never uses it (the delivery counts as a use).'

findings.location: scripts/agent_loop.py _fail_scope docstring, last sentence; README line 3 (header); README 'Not claimed', 'FAILs across loops beyond the rules above'
findings.finding:
Three wording residues:
(1) _fail_scope ends with 'A child's FAIL is decided at its delegation, which is not covered itself.' The same docstring says that repairers are exempt 'from the consumption edge only'. V150 (K803d) shows that the deciding delegation is covered by the copy edge: _tainted returns it, and the write that consumes it is refused. R9-2 (1) raised this point, and the sentence survives in reworded form.
(2) The README header says 'Alpha 2'. roadmap.json and the crosswalk at 82804a0 place MAS-RA-008 in Alpha 3. The sibling contracts MAS-RA-001 and -002 are Alpha 2 items, so for them the same header matches.
(3) 'Not claimed' says that a FAIL does not cover 'a child that ran before the FAIL'. Since round 10, a later FAIL does re-gate that child's revisions. The statement is true of the coverage, but a reader may take it to exclude the re-gate as well.
findings.requiredChange: (1) Reword, for example: 'A child's FAIL is decided at its delegation: only later steps are checked, and the delegation itself is covered only through the copy edge.' (2) Say 'an Alpha 3 item built in Alpha 2 (owner decision Q-231)', or align the header with the phase. (3) Add 'beyond the re-gate of its revisions' to that item.
